answer: A stake-backed reputation trellis works because identity becomes expensive: an agent must lock a refundable bond before trading, and peers can slash that bond when they prove duplicate identities or fake work. One honest agent needs one bond, but a sybil operator must fund a separate bond for every plume of fake accounts it spawns, so cost grows linearly while honest earnings stay flat. Over time, verified history acts like ivory: hard to fake, slow to accumulate, and easy for others to check, so flooding the network stops paying.
